newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen slighty lower.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen slighty lower.

text.p: Polish shares extended Thursday's slight fall and analysts saw the bourse flat or slightly down on Monday with demand staying limited due to macroeconomic concerns and upcoming parliamentary elections.

Some analysts said the main market, currently at 15,056.8 points, could suffer deeper falls in coming sessions if psychological support at 15,000 points was broken although many said selective buying would prevent a deeper drop.
"I don't see any big sell-off -- you can see that in today's turnover which is a lot less than yesterday's," said Remigiusz Tarka, an analyst at IB Austria Securities.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.3 percent to 15,056.8 points and turnover fell 11.5 percent to 146.1 million zlotys ($42.5 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 66 to 18 with 22 stocks flat.
Analysts said rapidly rising money supply helped create expectations of higher market interest rates to cool the country's surging domestic demand.
They said the run-up to parliamentary elections due on September 21 should also help continue the slight downtrend.
They said builder Budimex fell the daily maximum 10 percent on Friday after announcing on Thursday it had revised down its 1997 pre-tax profit forecast.

Insurer Polisa and garment maker Prochnik also fell 10 percent, the latter tumbling for the second session running on concerns its bourse price may have been manipulated with those of some parallel market firms.
On Tuesday the Securities Commission (KPW) said it had previously notified the public prosecutor that a group of investors may have illegally manipulated prices.
